news.title: McDonald's Is Using AI to Dynamically Price Its Burgers
If you've ever fallen down the rabbit hole of manhwa recap channels on YouTube — "The Weak…
news.author: hackaday@www.urbanmind.net
news.snippet: If you've ever fallen down the rabbit hole of manhwa recap channels on YouTube — "The Weakest Hunter Becomes the Strongest..." — you know the format: dramatic narration over panning comic panels, 10 minutes per video, millions of views. I kept wondering: could that entire pipeline be automated, running locally, with no subscriptions? That's how AniFlow was born — a self-hosted AI studio that takes manhwa/webtoon chapters and renders finished recap videos. It's open source (MIT): github.com/aashish254/Aniflow Here's how the pipeline works, and what was hard about each step. The pipeline Chapter ingestion. Paste a chapter URL or point at a local folder. The downloader grabs every page image in reading order. Panel detection (YOLOv8). Manhwa pages are vertical strips with irregular panel layouts. A trained YOLOv8 model detects panel boundaries so each panel can be cropped and sequenced for the video. This was the single hardest part — art styles vary wildly between series, and a detector trained on one artist's work falls apart on another's. Getting reliable detection across styles took the most iteration. Speech bubble detection + text extraction. A second detection pass finds speech bubbles and text regions. OCR pulls the dialogue out, which becomes the script for dialogue-recap mode. Bubble removal. For narrated mode, bubbles get removed and the art inpainted so panels look clean — like a friend telling you the story over the artwork. Doing this without leaving visible artifacts on detailed backgrounds was the second-hardest problem. Narration writing (LLM). The extracted story content goes to a local LLM (Ollama by default, with optional Gemini/Claude) with a prompt tuned for that dramatic recap-channel voice. It writes the narration script panel by panel. Voiceover (TTS). Multi-voice TTS — Edge TTS or Kokoro locally, ElevenLabs optionally — speaks the script. Different voices for narration vs. dialogue. Video rendering. Everything gets composited with FFmpeg: Ken Burns pan/zoom over panels, background music, watermarks, subtitles. Out comes an upload-ready vertical video. Two modes Dialogue recap — keeps the original speech bubbles visible; extracted dialogue becomes the audio. Closest to reading the chapter. Narrated recap — bubbles removed and inpainted; the AI narrates the story like a recap channel. Fully local by default The whole stack runs on your own machine: Ollama for narration, Edge TTS for voice, no API keys, no subscriptions, nothing leaves your computer. Cloud models are optional upgrades, not requirements. There's also a batch mode that processes 50+ chapters unattended — a full series to video overnight. What I'd do differently If I started over, I'd spend more time on the training data for panel detection up front instead of iterating on model tweaks — data diversity beat architecture fiddling every time. I'd also build the evaluation harness earlier: a small set of "golden" chapters across art styles to regression-test every change against. Try it Repo: github.com/aashish254/Aniflow (MIT). There's a web UI, a v0.1.0 release, and tutorial videos in the README. If you're into self-hosting, computer vision, or the manhwa scene — I'd love your feedback, and contributors are very welcome. # ai # automation # machinelearning # opensource # software # coding # development # engineering # inclusive # community How I Built an AI Studio That Turns Manhwa Chapters into Narrated Recap Videos

tele.title: Comin Asia and Nokia build sovereign AI infrastructure across Southeast Asia
tele.snippet: AI-ready data centres planned for Cambodia and Laos; Nokia partnership for regional sovereign AI infrastructure.

tele.title: Huawei expands Vietnam footprint through energy, AI, and 5G partnerships
tele.snippet: Partnerships spanning digital energy, AI, telecom infrastructure and industrial digitalization in Vietnam.

tele.title: Cellcard doubles 5G footprint to 500+ sites, targets 1,000 by end-July
tele.snippet: Cellcard CSX-listed operator: 500+ 5G BTS deployed since Jan 2026 launch; accelerating toward 1,000 sites across Phnom Penh and central region.

tele.title: Huawei and ZTE strengthen presence in Vietnam with new 5G network deal wins
tele.snippet: Huawei consortium ~$23M 5G equipment contract; Viettel targeting 20,000 new 5G base stations in 2025. 11,000+ stations deployed nationwide.

tele.title: EU warns Vietnam: Chinese 5G vendors may deter foreign investment
tele.snippet: Ericsson and Nokia on core; Huawei and ZTE winning RAN/antenna contracts. EU Commissioner Sikela: 5G is the new battlefield for trusted vendors.

tele.title: Viettel targets 98% population 5G coverage; adds 20,000 sites in 2026
tele.title_orig: Viettel hướng tới phủ sóng 5G tới 98% dân số
tele.snippet: Deputy CEO Le Quang Hieu at MWC 2026: ~30,000 5G SA sites by end-2025; planning +20,000 in 2026 for 98% coverage.

tele.title: Vietnam eyes new 5G deals with Chinese tech firms despite US warnings
tele.snippet: Mobifone in talks with Huawei; Viettel and VNPT signed 5G supply contracts with ZTE and Huawei. Ericsson and Nokia still supply core network.

tele.title: Vietnam pursues new 5G deals with China despite US warnings
tele.title_orig: Việt Nam nhắm thỏa thuận 5G mới với Trung Quốc, bất chấp cảnh báo của Mỹ
tele.snippet: BBC Vietnamese: Mobifone negotiating with Huawei; Viettel/VNPT already signed with ZTE and Huawei for 5G equipment.

tele.title: Despite US warnings, Vietnam plans more 5G contracts with Chinese vendors
tele.title_orig: 不顾美国警告 越南拟与中企签更多5G网络合约
tele.snippet: Zaobao: Mobifone tender favors Chinese firms; Huawei 5G gear seen near US Consulate in HCMC; follows Viettel/VNPT ZTE/Huawei deals.

tele.title: Viettel to trial 6G in 2028 with Qualcomm strategic alliance
tele.title_orig: Viettel sẽ thử nghiệm 6G vào năm 2028
tele.snippet: MWC 2026: Viettel joins Qualcomm 6G alliance; commercial 6G target from 2029; co-develop premium AI smartphones.

tele.title: Cambodia 5G trial: Cellcard leads download speeds in early Ookla tests
tele.title_orig: អ៊ីនធើណិត 5G សាកល្បងជំហានដំបូងនៅកម្ពុជា
tele.snippet: AMS Khmer: Ookla trial shows Cellcard 548 Mbps, Smart 336 Mbps, Metfone 218 Mbps; 1,500+ 5G sites by March 2026.

tele.title: 1,500 5G base stations deployed in Cambodia's 5G race so far
tele.snippet: Smart Axiata 674, Metfone (Viettel) 531, Cellcard 289 stations. Ministry accelerating mobile and FWA rollout.

tele.title: Vietnam 5G median speed tops 500 Mbps for the first time; Viettel leads at 617 Mbps
tele.title_orig: Mạng 5G Việt Nam lần đầu vượt 500 Mbps
tele.snippet: VNNIC i-Speed Jan 2026: national 5G median 594.81 Mbps; Viettel 617 Mbps vs VNPT 311 Mbps and MobiFone 188 Mbps.

tele.title: Cambodia launches 5G as all three mobile operators switch on networks
tele.snippet: Cellcard, Metfone and Smart launched 5G from Jan 2026. Phased rollout from Phnom Penh and 14 provinces.
